case_title: Sham @ Kishor Bhaskarrao Matkari v. State of Maharashtra
previous_criminal_record: No. Court found unblemished antecedents; no prior criminal activity shown by prosecution
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (brother of the deceased Manohar; sister-in-law and nephews/niece also family members); prior dispute over land/property
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; IPC s.307; IPC s.201 (acquitted under s.201 at trial)
weapon: None mentioned as a dangerous weapon; a large stone and a gas cylinder with tube were found near the body, but the court said no dangerous weapon was used
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured daughter PW-7; neighbour PW-1; landlord PW-3); medical (post-mortem PW-6 and PW-11); recovery (stone inside house); confession before Executive Magistrate
confession: Statement to Executive Magistrate (PW-16) recorded in hospital, treated as statement under s.164 CrPC; not a dying declaration; relied on by the Supreme Court
aggravating_circumstances: Killings of three persons and injuries to two children of one family; victims asleep and defenceless; brutality; High Court's list of aggravating circumstances (not adopted by the Supreme Court as grounds for death)
mitigating_circumstances: No pre-plan or pre-meditation; quarrel arose from land/property dispute; no dangerous weapon used; unblemished antecedents; accused was 28 and jobless; long custody (over 10 years, over 5 in death cell); no reason to think he cannot be reformed
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC: life imprisonment and fine Rs.25,000 (default 2 years RI); convicted under s.307 IPC: 7 years RI and fine Rs.1,000; acquitted under s.201 IPC
high_court_outcome: Accused's appeal dismissed (conviction upheld); State's appeal allowed; life imprisonment enhanced to death
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 (three deaths) and attempt to murder under IPC s.307 (conviction upheld; Supreme Court agreed with conviction under ss.302 and 307)
neutral_facts: The accused lived in a rented house with the victim (the accused's brother), the victim's wife and their three children. A neighbour living in an adjoining tenancy in the same building reported a quarrel between the accused and the victim at about 9.00 to 9.15 p.m., during which the accused said he would deal with the victim later. Around 3.00 to 3.30 a.m., the neighbour heard shouting, the cries of the victim's wife, the noise of beating and the groans of a small child from the house, and smelled gas leakage and something burning. The neighbour and the landlord went to the house and met the accused coming out, with blood on the hands and clothes, who said three thieves had entered and assaulted the family. Smoke was seen coming from the house, and the police were called. Officers found the victim and his wife dead, the wife partly burnt, and a large stone and a gas cylinder with tube near her body. Two children and a girl were injured, and one son later died in hospital. Doctors who conducted the post-mortems recorded injuries on the deceased. While in hospital, the accused made a statement to an Executive Magistrate admitting the killings and the injuries to the children. The injured daughter saw part of the occurrence. A stone was recovered from inside the house. The police registered a case, seized articles, and arrested the accused.
attempt_completion: Completed (three deaths); attempt also charged under s.307 for injuries to two children
physical_harm: Death of the victim (brother), the victim's wife and their son; injuries to two children; wife partly burnt
number_of_offences: 3 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.302 and s.307; s.201 was acquitted at trial)
premeditation_planning: Not found. The Supreme Court concluded there was no pre-plan or pre-meditation to eliminate the brother's family; the High Court had described the attack as pre-meditated
motive: Land/property dispute between the accused and the victim (accepted by the court)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the injured daughter (PW-7); neighbour and landlord evidence (PWs 1 and 3); post-mortem medical opinion (PWs 6 and 11); recovery of stone; accused's confession before Executive Magistrate (PW-16)
witness_credibility: Found credible; court saw no reason to disbelieve PW-7, PW-1, PW-3 and the confessional statement
post_offence_conduct: Told neighbours and police that three thieves had attacked the household; found with blood on hands and clothes; the High Court found this story false (as noted in the judgment)
custody_duration: In jail since 30.06.2001 (over 10 years); in death cell since 03.05.2006 (over 5 years)
trial_duration: offence: 28/29.06.2001; trial judgment: 04/05.03.2003; High Court: 03.05.2006; Supreme Court: 30.09.2011
legal_representation: Accused: Tara Chand Sharma, Mahabir Singh Mangla, Uma Datta, Kishan Datta and Neelam Sharma. State: Sushil Karanjkar, Sachin Patil, Sanjay Kharde, Sankar A Chillarge and Asha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: FIR registered (Ex.P-22 treated as FIR); investigation completed; accused arrested; charge-sheet laid; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 307, life imprisonment for murder; High Court: accused's appeal dismissed, State's appeal allowed, death sentence imposed; Supreme Court: conviction upheld, death set aside, life imprisonment restored
prosecution_argument: Death sentence justified given three deaths and injuries to two children of one family; the State relied on Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral
defence_argument: Several mitigating circumstances (including unblemished antecedents and absence of premeditation) mean death was not warranted; not a rarest of rare case
legal_principle_applied: Rarest of rare test; weighing of aggravating and mitigating circumstances per Bachan Singh and later decisions; death only where a rarest of rare case
precedent_relied_upon: Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral v. State of Maharashtra, JT 2011 (10) SC 465 (distinguished); Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, (1980) 2 SCC 684 (referred); Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab, (1983) 3 SCC 470 (referred); C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu, (2010) 9 SCC 567 (referred)
sentencing_rationale: Not a rarest of rare case; the High Court gave inadequate reasons for enhancement; no pre-plan, unblemished antecedents, no dangerous weapon, the accused cannot be shown to be a menace; trial court's life sentence restored
judicial_mitigating_factors: No pre-planning or pre-meditation; quarrel over land dispute; no dangerous weapon used; unblemished antecedents; no reason to think the accused cannot be reformed; not a menace to society; trial court's demeanour assessment favoured life sentence
judicial_aggravating_factors: Three deaths acknowledged; no other aggravating factor weighed by the Supreme Court
